The region enclosed by the curve $y=2{x}^{2},$ for $x\in [0,1],$ and the horizontal line $y=2$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/3b634be23e06f6038e00b91f27eadacd1d1bcc51516d741786cc433a1ce731ce.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=2{x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(2)-(2{x}^{2})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(4{x}^{4}-8{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
